description: Oracle for V4-C UNKNOWN FLOW GENERALIZATION. Tests whether agent finds vulnerability classes not present in V4-B training.
novelty: ReDoS is a completely different class from V4-B. It involves regex generation, not data flow. The agent has never seen ReDoS patterns in the V4-B/V4-B.1 training.

bugs.description: path-to-regexp outputs backtracking regular expressions when two parameters are in a single segment separated by something that is not a period. The generated regex has catastrophic backtracking, causing denial of service.
bugs.root_cause: safePattern() generates lookahead patterns that create exponential backtracking when two parameters are adjacent in a segment

exploit.impact: Event loop blocked for >1000x longer than safe regex
exploit.description: The negative lookahead (?:(?!-)[^/])+? causes exponential backtracking when the input contains repeated separators

fix.description: Version 8.0.0 removes the features that can cause ReDoS. Alternatively, provide custom regex for parameters after the first in a single segment.

non_vulnerabilities.reason: When the previous text contains a delimiter character, the pattern is safe because the delimiter acts as a natural boundary
Standard regex capture groups without lookahead are safe from catastrophic backtracking

evaluation_criteria.generalization_test: Agent has never seen ReDoS in V4-B. Can it detect a vulnerability in a completely different class using only system model analysis?
